Start-of-tick time base in the embedded path (interpreter and generated C), adopted by the controller under the user's 'fix all findings' go-ahead (2026-11-11, recommended option, reversible): every block in tick k sees t_k, continuous and discrete states publish their value at t_k and are updated to t_{k+1} after all outputs (Simulink output-then-update order, which the canvas already follows).

Bitwise and shift blocks work on int32 two's complement on every path (canvas, interpreter, C); the generated C performs the bit operations on uint32 casts and converts back, so every operation is defined behaviour. Adopted by the controller under the 'fix all' go-ahead; the canvas and the C already used int32, only the interpreter changes.

decisions.topic: out-of-domain math in the embedded path (XBV-086)
decisions.decision: Out-of-domain inputs (acos(2), atanh(1.5), (-8)^(1/3)) publish NaN and raise the numeric fault on every path, as the canvas (NaN + MATH_DOMAIN_ERROR) and Simulink-generated C (libm returns NaN) do; the documented 'deterministic fallback 0' of the signal-only fault policy is replaced by NaN + fault flag. Adopted by the controller under the 'fix all' go-ahead.

ADIA's Rate Limiter has an explicit initialCondition parameter (default 0) that Simulink's block lacks; it is the output before the first sample, y(-1) = IC. Ts > 0: y(0) = clamp(u(0), IC + falling Ts, IC + rising Ts); inherited/continuous sample time: y(0) = IC (no time has elapsed). This is the canvas behaviour, adopted for the embedded path.

Structural compile errors MULTIPLE_DRIVERS, DUPLICATE_BLOCK_ID, UNKNOWN_BLOCK_TYPE (error) and the fuzzy warning FUZZY_EMPTY_AGGREGATE (MATLAB 'no rules fired': output mid-range) are dedicated codes rather than reuses of BLOCK_RUNTIME_FAULT / MATH_DOMAIN_ERROR; each has a recipe and guidance.

The Clock block outputs the simulation time (Simulink Clock; the embedded path already did). The old square-wave behaviour remains available as WaveformGen type 'Square'; no lab, example or saved model used Clock.freq. Adopted by the controller under the 'fix all' go-ahead.

Fixed-step solvers (euler, ode2, ode3, rk4, ode5, ode14x) do not locate zero crossings, as Simulink with 'Enable zero-crossing detection for fixed-step simulation' off (its default): a block mode changes at a major step, the output grid stays k*h, and batch runs equal the live canvas step. Variable-step ode23, ode45 and ode23tb keep event location.

Recorded as a product limitation, not fixed in WP-21: state-machine variables stay scalar; vector/matrix signals work inside an X-Bridges model and cross the state-machine boundary element by element (one scalar variable per element). Building vector/matrix variables is a feature (model, interpreter, C generator, validator, UI) estimated at 1-2 days; reversible on request.

MatrixDiag, Diag, DiagExtract and ExtractDiag follow MATLAB diag: the input shape decides (a vector builds a diagonal matrix, a matrix gives its diagonal), as the embedded interpreter and generated C already did. The create/extract diagMode option is removed instead of enforced, so existing models and parity are unchanged. Reversible on request.

ROBOT_VACUUM_SLAM and ROBOT_VACUUM_MAPPING update their occupancy grids once per major step (Simulink discrete-update semantics), not at every solver stage; euler and rk4 now give the same grid. robot_vacuum_twin and robot_vacuum_full_system outputs change from step 0; both labs still run 2 s without errors and the map fills.

SolverOptions.stiffDetect and outputTimes are removed: no solver, screen or saved model uses them, Simulink and MATLAB ode45 have no stiffness diagnostic, and output times stay on the k * fixedStep grid with the stop time hit exactly. Reversible on request (outputTimes could later be implemented as Simulink 'Output times').

findings.summary: Mixed time base inside one embedded tick (interpreter and generated C): Clock, WaveformGen and UNIT_DELAY are evaluated at t_k, while Integrator, INTEGRATOR_CONTINUOUS and RATE_LIMITER publish their post-update state (C writes the post-update value, xbCGenerator.ts ~4094) and Step evaluates t_(k+1) (C uses state timers; smInterpreter advances timers before stepXBState, so a guard in tick k sees time (k+1) dt). The canvas uses t_k for everything. Which convention is right is an open decision (D9): 'outputs at the start of the tick' (Simulink major-step semantics, canvas) or 'outputs at the end of the tick' (what guards see today). Either way all blocks of one tick must use the same time. Merged XBV-085 (Step) into this finding after the WP-16 Opus verifier showed the C and timers share the embedded convention.
findings.fix: WP-21 batch F (merge after verifier review; reworks 64c1525d, 49bf3dbc, c5ca0ca7).

Separate convention question: fallback NaN (canvas, Simulink) or 0 (embedded contract).

findings.summary: Robertson problem: ode23tb stops at step 1 with STIFF_SOLVER_NONFINITE when a Newton iterate overflows, instead of rejecting the step and retrying smaller (MATLAB ode23tb treats a failed Newton iteration as a step failure). Found by the WP-21 E4 verifier.
findings.fix: WP-21 batch E5: a non-finite Newton iterate or stage derivative at a trial state is a failed ode23tb step (h/4, retry down to hMin); only a non-finite derivative at the accepted state stops the run. Robertson to t = 40 within 1e-4 relative of the reference.

findings.summary: Fixed-step euler, ode2, ode3, rk4, ode5 (Solvers.ts) and ode14x (StiffSolver.ts ~384) compute zcPrev = getZeroCrossings(t, statesPrev) without computeOutputs first, so gatherInputs reads the trial-end signals, the sign change is never seen and bracketZeroCrossing is never called (0 calls on the Switch test model); bracketZeroCrossing has the same flaw internally. ode45/ode23 use their own locateEvent and are not affected. Found by the WP-21 E4 verifier.
findings.fix: WP-21 batch E5, decision D15: the zero-crossing event branch is removed from the fixed-step batch solvers (euler..ode5, ode14x) and engine.bracketZeroCrossing is gone; batch grid is k*h and batch equals live. ode23/ode45/ode23tb keep event location.

findings.summary: PT_AUTOMATED_MANUAL_TRANSMISSION under rk4 at 1e-3 never locks within 0.05 s (DiffTrq +-1600 chatter) and locks late (0.0115 s vs 0.0019 s) at 1e-4; same on the base. Simulink locks the clutch with a zero crossing on slip; depends on XBV-186. Found by the WP-21 E4 verifier.
findings.fix: WP-21 batch E5: PT_DISC_CLUTCH and the AMT/DCT clutches are hybrid: lock decided at major steps when the slip is within omega_tol or changed sign since the previous major step and |T_lock| <= Ts, friction direction held in minor steps; live ode45/ode23 make the step ending at a located event a major step. rk4 1e-3 / 1e-4 lock within 2 steps of ode23tb; disc clutch t* = 0.04386 s matched; live variable-step results equal the base.

findings.summary: robot_vacuum_twin: the first run in a fresh process differs from later runs in robot_nav.nav_stats and robot_slam.* (Math.random seeded), so a block keeps state across runs (module-level state not reset on Play). Found by the WP-21 F3 verifier.
findings.fix: WP-21 batch R: root cause was the module-level g_isMatlabActive in BlockDefinitions.ts (latches the 12 m map once a lidar hit or pose leaves the 6 m house, reset only by three blocks the twin lab does not contain). XbridgesEngine.compile() now calls resetTwinRunState(), so every run starts from the initial grid mode; robot_vacuum_twin runs are identical run after run (verified with a 3-run reproduction).

findings.summary: ROBOT_VACUUM_MOTOR pwm_duty reads |u| <= 1 as a duty cycle and larger values as volts; the port unit is 'V' since WP-21 K (fits the labs), but one port mixes two meanings. Simulink-style: one meaning per port. Found by the WP-21 K verifier.
findings.fix: WP-21 batch R: pwm_duty is a voltage command, V_in = clamp(u, -max(V_bat,0), max(V_bat,0)); the 0.1 V floor on V_bat is gone; label V_cmd. Commands below 1 V were driven 12x too hard before (di/dt at rest 1200 vs 100 for 0.5 V).

findings.summary: Canvas LOW_PASS_FILTER, HIGH_PASS_FILTER and MOVING_AVERAGE are not element-wise on a vector input: a 3-vector gives the scalar [0] (filters) or [null] (moving average) at step 0, while the embedded path and Simulink (Lowpass/Highpass Filter, Moving Average are element-wise) give a 3-vector. Pinned under XBV-018/XBV-068 in xbTriParity until WP-21 round 5.
findings.fix: WP-21 batch D2: LOW_PASS_FILTER, HIGH_PASS_FILTER (continuous and discrete) and MOVING_AVERAGE are element-wise with per-element state; verified against the closed forms per element; scalar results bit-identical to the base.

findings.summary: Canvas RATE_LIMITER outputs 0 at t = 0 for a constant 0.7 input with rising/falling limits 0.1 per step; decision D12 (initial condition y(-1) = IC = 0) gives clamp(0.7, 0 +/- 0.1) = 0.1, which the embedded path outputs. Pinned under XBV-018 in xbTriParity until WP-21 round 5.
findings.fix: WP-21 batch D2: with an explicit Ts the first Rate Limiter output is clamp(u, IC - F*Ts, IC + R*Ts) (D12); with an inherited sample time y(0) = IC, as the interpreter. Rate Limiter is element-wise.

findings.summary: RATE_LIMITER with vector slew rates: p.risingSlewRate * dt is NaN, so limiting is silently skipped and u passes through (also on the base). Simulink Rate Limiter accepts only scalar rates; a vector rate must be a diagnostic or element-wise. Found by the WP-21 D2 verifier.
findings.fix: WP-21 batch D3: RATE_LIMITER takes scalar or vector rising/falling rates applied per element (D12 kept, scalar results identical on 300 random models); a size mismatch stops the run at the first step with BLOCK_RUNTIME_FAULT; modelChecks checks rates element-wise. The embedded path refuses vector rates at validation (XB_PARAMETER_INVALID).

findings.summary: The embedded validator refuses RATE_LIMITER vector slew rates with the generic message 'risingSlewRate must be >= 0...' instead of saying that vector rates are not supported by Generate C (the canvas accepts them since XBV-192). Found by the WP-21 D3 verifier.
findings.fix: WP-21: the embedded validator refuses vector Rate Limiter slew rates with 'Generate C supports only scalar slew rates (the canvas accepts per-element vector rates)', keeps the other parameter checks in the same pass, and treats one-element [2] / '[2]' as scalars.

findings.summary: A RATE_LIMITER slew rate given as the one-element array [2] passes the embedded validator, but xbInterpreter.parameter and xbCGenerator.scalarParameter read only numbers and silently fall back to the default rate 1 (0.1/0.2/0.3 instead of 0.2/0.4/0.6 per tick at dt 0.1, u = 10); the string '[2]' works. Generate C produces the wrong rate with no diagnostic. Same on the base. Found by the WP-21 XBV-193 verifier.
findings.fix: WP-21 batch S: the shared embedded readers (xbInterpreter.parameter, xbCGenerator.scalarParameter) read a one-element array or string and a plain numeric string as a scalar; [2], '[2]' and '2' give 0.2/0.4/0.6 on the canvas, the interpreter and compiled C.

findings.summary: src/utils/stateMachine smDifferential: the state-timer Step value is [0,2,2,2] where [0,2,2,5] is expected (not an environment issue; fails on the base too). Found by the WP-21 XBV-193 verifier; root cause not yet analysed.
findings.fix: WP-21 batch S: not a product defect. The smDifferential Step expectation predated D9 (fb4c4bd5): with 10 ms ticks and 2 ms euler substeps evaluated at their start, the published values are 2, 2, 2, 5 (8/18/28/38 ms); the test now runs 4 ticks and expects [0,2,2,2,5]; interpreter = C.

findings.summary: An empty RATE_LIMITER slew rate [] / '[]' is refused by the embedded validator with the 'vector slew rates' message although it has no elements (the base silently ran it at rate 1); the message should say the rate is empty. A legacy fallingLimit '[1,2]' gets only the generic message because the factory turns it into NaN first. Found by the WP-21 XBV-193 verifier.
findings.fix: WP-21 batch S: an empty slew rate [] / '[]' is refused with an 'empty' message (XB_PARAMETER_INVALID).

findings.summary: RATE_LIMITER legacy aliases risingLimit / fallingLimit set to '' pass the embedded validator as Number('') = 0, while the readers fall back to the default 1 (interpreter = C, so no parity gap); an empty alias should be refused like an empty slew rate. Older than WP-21 batch S. Found by the batch S verifier.
findings.fix: WP-21 batch E6: blank risingLimit / fallingLimit aliases are refused by the embedded validator with the 'empty' message.

findings.summary: 44 blocks (CLARKE/PARK/INVERSE_* transforms, AC_MOTOR_PID_CONTROL, FIELD_ORIENTED_CONTROL, FUZZY_MF_GAUSSMF/SIGMF, ROBOT_VACUUM_*, DEM_BOND_FABRIC, LMS/NEURAL, SVPWM_CORE, ...) coerce a vector, matrix or ragged input with Number() and output NaN with only the generic NUMERICAL_INSTABILITY warning (858 type.port:shape cases); Simulink computes element-wise or reports a dimension error. Found by WP-03b (xbUniversalB.test.ts, ratchet tests/fixtures/xbridges/universal-gaps-b.json), reproduced by the verifier.
findings.fix: WP-21 batch U2: FUZZY_MF_GAUSSMF / SIGMF are element-wise (Fuzzy Logic Toolbox); 42 blocks with fixed-meaning inputs (motor control, Clarke/Park and their inverses, robot vacuum, DEM, LMS/neural, SVPWM_CORE) refuse a wrong input shape with a block error naming the port and the expected shape (FIXED_SHAPE_INPUTS, every fixed-meaning port declared). All 11 labs bit-identical; scalar results bit-identical on 46 types.

findings.summary: Determinant throws for non-square / vector / 1xn / nx1 / ragged input and Transpose for ragged input, instead of a dimension diagnostic (BlockDefinitions.ts / VectorUtils.ts). Found by WP-03b (xbUniversalB.test.ts, ratchet tests/fixtures/xbridges/universal-gaps-b.json), reproduced by the verifier.
findings.fix: WP-21 batch U2: Determinant (non-square, vector, ragged) and Transpose (ragged) return a dimension block error instead of throwing; scalar and 1x1 stay valid for Determinant (MATLAB det).

findings.summary: parameterSchema lists representation continuous|discrete for TRANSFER_FUNCTION, ZERO_POLE_GAIN, LAPLACE_TRANSFORM and DISCRETE_TRANSFER_FUNCTION; the factories fix the domain (as Simulink's separate blocks do) and the panel hides the parameter, so the schema option list is wrong. Found by WP-03b (xbUniversalB.test.ts, ratchet tests/fixtures/xbridges/universal-gaps-b.json), reproduced by the verifier.
findings.fix: WP-21 batch U1: parameterSchema lists one representation per transfer-function block (continuous for TRANSFER_FUNCTION, ZERO_POLE_GAIN, LAPLACE_TRANSFORM; discrete for DISCRETE_TRANSFER_FUNCTION), matching the factories; STATE_SPACE keeps both.

findings.summary: FLUX_REFERENCE mode field_weakening gives the same output as constant (silent no-op; the code comment says not implemented, BlockDefinitions.ts ~3883). Found by WP-03b (xbUniversalB.test.ts, ratchet tests/fixtures/xbridges/universal-gaps-b.json), reproduced by the verifier.
findings.fix: WP-21 batch U1: FLUX_REFERENCE has a speed input and base_speed; field_weakening gives value for |w| <= base_speed and value*base_speed/|w| above it; default value stays 0.

findings.summary: MatrixDiag, Diag, DiagExtract and ExtractDiag ignore diagMode create|extract; VectorUtils.diag decides from the input shape (silent no-op). Found by WP-03b (xbUniversalB.test.ts, ratchet tests/fixtures/xbridges/universal-gaps-b.json), reproduced by the verifier.
findings.fix: WP-21 batch U1, decision D17: MatrixDiag / Diag / DiagExtract / ExtractDiag follow MATLAB diag (vector -> diagonal matrix, matrix -> diagonal); the misleading diagMode option is removed from factory, schema, panel, node badge and help; saved models with a stray diagMode still load and run.

findings.summary: Discrete sample hits accumulate nextTime += Ts: with Ts 0.1 and h 0.01 from t = 0 the hit at t = 5094.2 s (tick 509420) and every later hit fire one tick late, so the outputs are wrong (XbridgesEngine.updateDiscreteStates). Found by WP-03b (xbUniversalB.test.ts, ratchet tests/fixtures/xbridges/universal-gaps-b.json), reproduced by the verifier.
findings.fix: WP-21 batch E6: discrete hits are scheduled on integer indices (hit n at n*Ts, per-block hitIndex), never by nextTime += Ts; the hit test tolerates only the floating-point error of t (1e-9 + 64 eps |t|, 1.4e-7 s at 1e7 s); first hit n0 = ceil(start/Ts - 1e-6). Verified on the grid at starts 0..1e7 s, 1e6-tick runs and worker resume.

findings.summary: Generated C member names are not unique in the first 63 characters (C99 5.2.4.1) for ids that differ only later; smCIdentifierPolicy is not applied to members (xbCGenerator.ts). Found by WP-03b (xbUniversalB.test.ts, ratchet tests/fixtures/xbridges/universal-gaps-b.json), reproduced by the verifier.
findings.fix: WP-21 batch U3 (4 reworks): generated C identifiers derived from model ids are shortened at their name builders (limitCIdentifierLength: 54-char prefix + '_' + 8 hex SHA-256; cStateIndexSymbol for every state index); xbCGenerator's text mapping skips comments, string/char literals and variable members; harnesses use the product's builders. Short ids give 738 byte-identical files across 6 option sets; long block, state and variable ids compile (gcc, clang -Werror) and give simulator = C = standalone traces.

findings.summary: FUZZY_INFERENCE_SYSTEM.orMethod (max|probor) is stored but never read: both give 0.083979 while andMethod changes the output (BlockDefinitions.ts ~10551). Found by WP-03b (xbUniversalB.test.ts, ratchet tests/fixtures/xbridges/universal-gaps-b.json), reproduced by the verifier.
findings.fix: WP-21 batch U1: FUZZY_INFERENCE_SYSTEM.orMethod (max | probor) combines the antecedents of OR rules; rule aggregation stays max (MATLAB AggregationMethod).

findings.summary: 16 panel enums outside parameterSchema accept unknown and wrong-case values silently (CLARKE_TRANSFORM.mode runs an unknown value as power-invariant; PWM_GENERATOR.carrierType; THREE_PHASE_PWM.method; CFD_DEM_SURROGATE_LEARNER.mode; Diag*.diagMode; FUZZY_INFERENCE_SYSTEM type/andMethod/orMethod/defuzzMethod; FUZZY_RULE operator/implication; FUZZY_AND/OR method; FUZZY_DEFUZZIFY.method, where 'zz_unknown' and 'MOM' silently give the centroid); Simulink refuses an invalid dialog value (PARAMETER_OPTION_INVALID). Found by WP-03b (xbUniversalB.test.ts, ratchet tests/fixtures/xbridges/universal-gaps-b.json), reproduced by the verifier.
findings.fix: WP-21 batch U1: 16 panel option parameters (CLARKE mode, PWM carrierType, THREE_PHASE_PWM method, CFD_DEM mode, FIS type/and/or/defuzz, FUZZY_RULE operator/implication, FUZZY_AND/OR/DEFUZZIFY method) are in parameterSchema with the panel's values; unknown and wrong-case values are refused at compile. No lab uses a value outside the lists.

findings.summary: XbridgesEngine.compile first-hit margin n0 = ceil(start/Ts - 1e-6) is below the ulp of start/Ts from about 1e11 ticks (start 1.8e7 s at Ts 1e-4, 1.3e8 s at Ts 1e-3): the first hit at an on-grid start is skipped in 0.8-7% of random starts. Suggested margin max(1e-6, 64 eps |start/Ts|). Found by the WP-21 E6 verifier.
findings.fix: WP-21 batch E7: first-hit margin max(1e-6, 64 eps |start/Ts|) ticks; 0 misses from 1e9 to 1e13 ticks.

findings.summary: Scope sampleTime decimation compares time - lastSampleTime with an absolute 1e-9 (BlockDefinitions.ts ~3107): at start 1e8 s, h 0.01, Ts 0.1 it logs 12000 of 20000 samples (0.2 s gaps); clean at 0, 1e6, 1e7 s. Needs the integer-index grid of XBV-307. Found by the WP-21 E6 verifier.
findings.fix: WP-21 batch E7: Scope sample-time logging on the integer-index grid (sample n at the first time >= n*Ts, tolerance 1e-9 + 64 eps |t|); start-0 logs unchanged.

findings.summary: PWM carrier phase += dt*f (BlockDefinitions.ts ~447) accumulates a bounded error (5e-12 after 1e6 steps from 0, 3.6e-8 at 1e8 s); a duty exactly equal to the carrier value (e.g. 0.3) can flip the gate on a tie. Derive the phase from t (frac(f t + phase0)). Found by the WP-21 E6 verifier.
findings.fix: WP-21 batch E7: the PWM / three-phase PWM / SVPWM carrier phase is a function of time: on the solver grid frac(frac(f*start) + i*(f*h)) from the integer tick with error-free (Dekker) products, off grid frac(f*t) of the exact product; ties decided at 1e-12 cycles (documented). 0 non-tie edge differences versus an exact BigInt oracle; invalid frequency is a block error instead of a silent 50 Hz.

findings.summary: A Scope with sampleTime 0.1 over [0, 2] logs 20 samples; Simulink logs 21 (both endpoints, t = 2 included). Same on the base. Found by the WP-21 E7 verifier.
findings.fix: WP-21 batch E8: batch solvers end with engine.finishAtStopTime (outputs and the discrete update at t_final, as Simulink's last major step), so a Scope with Ts logs both endpoints (21 samples for Ts 0.1 on [0, 2]); no double logging; batch equals live.

findings.summary: The 'positive' parameter kind rejects 0, negatives, NaN, text and empty at compile time but accepts Infinity, which then fails only at run time (for example PWM frequency). 'positive' (and 'nonnegative') must reject non-finite values with a PARAMETER_* diagnostic. Found by the WP-21 E7 verifier.
findings.fix: WP-21 batch E8: the positive and nonnegative parameter kinds refuse +/-Infinity and NaN at compile (PARAMETER_OUT_OF_RANGE); no factory default is non-finite; parameters that may be inf (stop time, saturation limits) use other kinds.

findings.summary: Generated C names that are not unique within their first 63 characters (C99 5.2.4.1) for long model ids, identical on the base: SM_ST_<enum>_Entry / _Exit / _During when the state enum name is 63 characters; SM_Data_t variable members whose ids share 63 characters (count / counter); MCAL_CH_<channel> macros. Found by the WP-21 U3 verifier; out of scope of XBV-308 (X-Bridges member names).
findings.fix: WP-21 batch U4: one builder per name family in smCIdentifierPolicy (cDataMemberName for SM_Data_t members, cStateActionSymbol = limit(enum + '_' + phase), cMcalChannelMacro), used by the C generator, semantic builder and validator, host test suite, xbCGenerator, AUTOSAR report and the HIL generator; no two names share 63 characters; long-variable HIL packages compile (Generic gcc -std=c99 -Wall -Werror); validator diagnostics unchanged; short-id output byte-identical except two pre-existing fixes (xb6StepFixture host suite now compiles; Generic main_hil.c declares usleep via _DEFAULT_SOURCE).

findings.summary: The worker engine snapshot keeps block states but not the discrete hit indices (hitIndex / nextTick): a run 0..2 resumed 2..4 from the snapshot repeats the hit at t = 2 (discrete integrator 10 instead of 9; DELAY buffer differs). Pre-existing; the app never sends a snapshot back to the worker today, but the protocol supports it. Found by the WP-21 E8 verifier.
findings.fix: WP-21 batch U4: the worker engine snapshot carries each discrete block's sampleGrid (hitIndex, nextTick) and restores it on compile with a snapshot; resumed runs equal uninterrupted runs (<= 4.4e-16) for UNIT_DELAY, DELAY, RATE_LIMITER and Scope at hit and non-hit resume times; old snapshots fall back.

findings.summary: Generic HIL hal_drivers.c: clang -Werror reports 4 unused static functions (HAL_UART / HAL_SPI helpers); gcc accepts it. Pre-existing on the base. Found by the WP-21 U4 verifier.
findings.fix: WP-21: the Generic HIL package emits its UART/SPI channel helpers, input / output simulation arrays and pin helper only when a channel uses them; 14 channel configurations compile and link with gcc and clang -std=c99 -Wall -Wextra -Werror; all other targets byte-identical.

findings.summary: The worker never runs hybrid discrete updates: the client strips updateDiscrete (XBV-047) and the XbridgesEngine constructor re-creates only execute / evaluateDerivatives / ZeroCrossingFn, so PT_AUTOMATED_MANUAL_TRANSMISSION, PT_DUAL_CLUTCH_TRANSMISSION and PT_DISC_CLUTCH differ from the main thread from step 0 (the clutch never locks). Found by WP-14b (xbWorkerB.test.ts), reproduced by the verifier.
findings.fix: WP-21 batch W1: the XbridgesEngine constructor re-creates every function member the block's factory defines (called with the block's own params), so the worker runs updateDiscrete; AMT / DCT / disc clutch worker = main thread sample for sample; 212 library types identical live vs JSON-stripped.

findings.summary: The worker hangs on AMT / DCT under ode23 and ode23tb and on PT_DISC_CLUTCH under ode23tb (canvas freezes); a consequence of XBV-405 only (with updateDiscrete the same models finish in < 60 ms). Found by WP-14b (xbWorkerB.test.ts), reproduced by the verifier.
findings.fix: WP-21 batch W1: consequence of XBV-405, resolved with it; the worker no longer hangs on the hybrid PT blocks under ode23 / ode23tb.

findings.summary: BLOCK_LIBRARY keys 'Integrator' and 'INTEGRATOR' differ only in case; the engine's case-insensitive rebuild (XbridgesEngine.ts ~140) gives the worker Integrator's execute for an INTEGRATOR block, so output limits and reset are ignored (limited x 1.0 instead of 0.2). The main-thread canvas looks types up exactly and is not affected. Found by WP-14b (xbWorkerB.test.ts), reproduced by the verifier.
findings.fix: WP-21 batch W1: block types resolve by exact key first, then case-insensitively; Integrator / INTEGRATOR is the only case-only pair; other case variants in saved models still load.

findings.summary: The main thread hangs (killed at 20 s) on a chattering sliding mode under ode23, ode45 and ode23tb: Integrator (IC 0.0123) -> SWITCH (x >= 0 ? -1 : +1) -> Integrator; rk4 finishes in 5 ms. AdaptiveSolver.locateEvent (~216) and StiffSolver (~532) have no cap on events or steps; Simulink stops with an error after the consecutive zero-crossings limit. Found by WP-14b (xbWorkerB.test.ts), reproduced by the verifier.
findings.fix: WP-21 batch S2: Simulink-style consecutive zero-crossing limit (1000 crossings within a tiny window of each other, ZERO_CROSSING_CHATTER error naming the block) in AdaptiveSolver and StiffSolver, live and batch; internal step caps (STIFF_SOLVER_STEP_TOO_SMALL). The sliding mode stops in ~0.2 s; PWM at 20 and 200 kHz is not flagged.

findings.summary: A faulted batch under ode5, ode23 or ode45 leaves a partial step committed (x = 0.554 / 0.54, not a whole number of steps). Found by WP-14b (xbWorkerB.test.ts), reproduced by the verifier.
findings.fix: WP-21 batch S2: a faulted step commits nothing; live steps and fixed-step batch loops deep-copy block states (cloneState) before the step and restore them on a fault; ode5 / ode23 / ode45 leave the step-start state.

findings.summary: A faulted step under ode2, ode3 or rk4 is committed (x = 0.6) while the reported simulationTime stays at the step start (0.25). Found by WP-14b (xbWorkerB.test.ts), reproduced by the verifier.
findings.fix: WP-21 batch S2: under ode2 / ode3 / rk4 a faulted step commits nothing, so state and reported time both stay at the step start.

findings.summary: The worker engine snapshot lacks published signal values, so a resume between sample hits publishes the initial output until the next hit (UNIT_DELAY, INTEGRATOR_DISCRETE, DISCRETE_TRANSFER_FUNCTION, AIR_FRYER_LEARNING_MODEL). No product code sends a snapshot to the worker today. Found by WP-14b (xbWorkerB.test.ts), reproduced by the verifier.
findings.fix: WP-21 batch W1: the worker snapshot carries the published values of sampled blocks; restoreHeldOutput restores them and the ZOH cache, so a resume between hits publishes the held output; old snapshots fall back; non-sampled blocks are never overwritten.

findings.summary: Live ode45 integrates a 30 % duty 20 kHz PWM to 0.0673 over 0.2 s instead of 0.06 (12 % high); pinned in xbWp21Round7. Found while writing the WP-21 S2 rework acceptance; same on the base.
findings.fix: WP-21 E9: blocks with time-scheduled discontinuities (every PWM carrier, THREE_PHASE_PWM, SVPWM_GATE_GENERATOR, WaveformGen Square, Step) declare nextEventTime; ode23 / ode45 / ode23tb land on a +-1e-12 s bracket around each edge and cross it with one explicit Euler step of every state, live and batch. 20 kHz 30 % PWM integrates to 0.06 within 5e-8.

findings.summary: ode23tb integrates a 30 % duty 20 kHz PWM to about 0 (batch 0.0002 over 1 s instead of 0.3; live 0.0013 over 0.2 s instead of 0.06); pinned in xbWp21Round7. Same on the base.
findings.fix: WP-21 E9: as XBV-409; exact-integral acceptance (xbWp21Round8, 72 cases, |error| <= 2e-6) over partial periods, duty steps, duty 0 / 1, sawtooth, inverse sawtooth and square carriers, SVPWM and WaveformGen Square.

findings.summary: Variable-step solvers mis-integrate a PWM-driven integrator broadly (controller acceptance, oracle duty * 1 s = 0.3, fixed-step rk4 converges to 0.300): at 50 Hz ode45 0.238, ode23 0.248, ode23tb 0.006; at 500 Hz and 1 kHz (minStep 1e-4) values from 0.002 to 1.0. Same without S2. Generalises XBV-409/410.
findings.fix: WP-21 E9: as XBV-409; 1000 / 500 / 50 Hz accurate at any minStep. Events of different blocks closer than hMin are landed one after another; an event at the stop time keeps the whole last pulse (xbWp21Round9).

findings.summary: The ZERO_CROSSING_CHATTER window includes 10 * minStep, so with a user minStep of 1e-3 a 1 kHz PWM is flagged as chatter at t = 0.62; Simulink would report a minimum-step violation. Build the window from the event-location tolerance and machine precision only. Found by the WP-21 S2 verifier.
findings.fix: WP-21 E9: the chatter window no longer widens with minStep; STIFF_SOLVER_STEP_TOO_SMALL only when one block's own events are closer than hMin; genuine sliding modes still give ZERO_CROSSING_CHATTER.

findings.summary: ROBOT_VACUUM_BATTERY execute mutates its committed state in place (BlockDefinitions.ts ~7181), the only library block that does; batch ode45 / ode23 do not restore in-place mutations on a fault, so its final state shows 100 instead of the last committed 100.000005 (outputs unchanged). Fix the block to copy its state and add a contract test that deep-freezes every block's state during a step, so the 256-element copy cap in cloneState can go. Found by the WP-21 S2 verifier. Controller contract test: ROBOT_VACUUM_BATTERY, ROBOT_VACUUM_MAPPING, ROBOT_VACUUM_OBSTACLE_AVOIDANCE and ROBOT_VACUUM_SLAM execute write to a frozen state.
findings.fix: WP-21 E9: ROBOT_VACUUM_BATTERY, MAPPING, OBSTACLE_AVOIDANCE and SLAM copy their state instead of writing it in place; contract test deep-freezes every block's state during a step. SLAM / MAPPING grids update once per major step (D18).

findings.summary: Batch ode23 / ode45 reuse the first-same-as-last stage across a located event (AdaptiveSolver.ts ~354): RELAY and SWITCH driven by a sine integrate with errors -2.66e-5 to 1.47e-2 at default tolerances (oracles 1 and 1 - 4 asin(0.3)/pi). ode23tb and live are exact; the verifier's one-line probe (fresh k1 after an event) gives <= 2e-12. Pinned in xbEngineB (4 it.fails). Found by WP-13b.
findings.fix: WP-21 E10: the first stage is re-evaluated after a landed event (k1Valid false after a sliver step that reaches the event); batch ode23 / ode45 RELAY and SWITCH errors 2.7e-5..1.5e-2 -> 1e-13..2e-12; a crossing landing exactly on a normal step end goes the same way (-2.58e-4 -> 4.6e-13).

findings.summary: Live variable-step: a zero crossing whose step starts exactly on the crossing (base value exactly 0) is skipped (zeroCrossingGuard.ts ~31), so DEADZONE with its limit hit exactly on the output grid (u = t - 1, limit 0.5 at t = 1.5) holds the inside region for the whole step: error h^2/2 = 5e-5 on ode23 / ode45 / ode23tb; limit 1.505 is exact. Pinned in xbEngineB (6 it.fails). Found by WP-13b.
findings.fix: WP-21 E10: crossedOrTouched counts a zero base value followed by a finite non-zero value; live DEADZONE on the grid -5e-5 -> 3.5e-16; no double count (steps land past hi + 2 tol), no chatter on touches or functions resting at 0.

findings.summary: Algebraic loop y = 1 + g y with g = 1e10 or 1e300 (finite solution -1/(g-1)) returns Infinity with only ALGEBRAIC_LOOP and NUMERICAL_INSTABILITY warnings and the run continues; expected the finite solution or the fatal ALGEBRAIC_LOOP_NOT_CONVERGED (Simulink stops on a loop it cannot solve). Pinned in xbEngineB (1 it.fails). Found by WP-13b.
findings.fix: WP-21 E10: a non-finite Gauss-Seidel sweep falls back to Newton from the pre-sweep values, the finite-difference step scales with max(1, |z|), a non-finite F or z is a fatal ALGEBRAIC_LOOP_NOT_CONVERGED; y = 1 + g y gives -1/(g-1) for g = 1e10 and 1e300; nonlinear loops y = C - k y^2 (C up to 1e12) within 1.2e-7 where the base gave Infinity.

findings.summary: algTol and maxIter of the algebraic loop solver are honoured by the engine (engine.options) but the canvas never passes them (solverOptionsForRun) and the workspace has no field for them; Simulink exposes the algebraic loop solver tolerance in the configuration parameters. Decide whether to expose them or document the fixed defaults (1e-6, 100). Found by WP-13b.

Algebraic loop y = 1 + 1e10 y under rk4: from step 2 the loop value is -8.27e-8 (exact -1e-10) and the gain output -827 (exact -1), no diagnostic; ode45 is exact. The loop value meets algTol*(1+|y|), but with gain 1e10 the residual test accepts a value 827x off (ill-conditioning: the convergence test should be on the residual scaled by the loop gain, or warn). Before E10 the result was Infinity. Found by the E10 verifier.
findings.fix: WP-21 E11: a Gauss-Seidel sweep counts as settled only when its change meets algTol and is 0 or no larger than the previous sweep's change; a non-contracting loop (|g| > 1) goes to Newton. g = 1e10 rk4: gain output -827.4 -> -1.000000083 at every step; g = 1e6 exact; sweeps +1.3 % over 885 loop-bearing tests.

findings.summary: RELAY (switchOn 0.25, switchOff 0) on u = (t-1)^2, which touches switchOff at t = 1 without crossing it: batch ode23 / ode45 / ode23tb never switch the relay off (integral off by 0.5 against an oracle that switches at u <= switchOff), while live switches off because t = 1 is a grid point. Simulink zero-crossing detection also locates only sign changes, so the batch result may be the Simulink one: decide against a Simulink golden (WP-15); live and batch must agree either way. Found by the E10 verifier, same before and after E10.

DEADZONE [-1, 0] of u = (t-1)^2 (tangent touch of the upper limit at t = 1) under batch ode23tb at default tolerances errs by 2.55e-4 (ode23 / ode45 exact); confirm the oracle with a Simulink golden (WP-15). Found by the E10 verifier, same before and after E10.

Algebraic loop convergence is judged on the residual (sweep change, Newton residual), not on the solution: y = c(t) + q y under rk4 misses algTol*(1+|y|) on the solution by about 1/(1-q): q = 0.9 6x, 0.99 100x, 0.9999 1e4x, 0.999999 (c = 1 + 0.1 t) error 0.167 relative; nonlinear y = c + y - 1e-6 y^2 250x; no diagnostic. Same before and after E11. Simulink iterates until the step is small. Found by the E11 verifier.

y = c + y - k y^2 with k = 1e-8 (solution 1e4) gives a fatal ALGEBRAIC_LOOP_NOT_CONVERGED at t = 0: the Newton Jacobian 2 k y is 0 at the starting guess 0. Same before and after E11. Found by the E11 verifier.

Live ode23 / ode45 have no initial-step heuristic: the first internal step is the output step (AdaptiveSolver.ts ~412). For ode23 on x' = -x with dt = 1 the Bogacki-Shampine estimate is exactly 0 at h lambda = -1 (err = -z^3 (1+z)/48), so the step is accepted: x(1) = 1/3 (-9.4 %), and the step hint keeps h = 1 (x(10) -62.7 %). Simulink starts from a tolerance-based initial step capped by MaxStep. Pinned in xbSolversB. Found by WP-12b.
findings.fix: WP-21 E13: MATLAB hinitial initial step (rh = ||f0 ./ max(|y0|, AbsTol/RelTol)||_inf / (0.8 RelTol^pow), pow 1/5 ode45, 1/3 ode23), capped by maxStep and the output step, at the start of a live run and whenever the hint is invalid; the hint is dropped after a step accepted with a zero estimate. Live ode23 x' = -x dt 1: x(10) 1.69e-5 -> 4.53992e-5 (exact 4.539993e-5). PWM step counts unchanged.

findings.summary: maxStep does not cap the first step: live h0 = min(hint ?? dt, dt) ignores hMax (ode23 one step of 1.0 with maxStep 0.01), batch h0 = span / 50 = 0.2 (981 steps for T = 10, maxStep 0.01, instead of at least 1000). Pinned in xbSolversB. Found by WP-12b.
findings.fix: WP-21 E13: every step, the first included, is capped by maxStep, live and batch (maxStep 0.01: live 100 steps, batch 1000).

findings.summary: Batch ode23 / ode45 accept a step at minStep that misses the tolerance with no diagnostic (AdaptiveSolver.ts ~298, accept = ... || (batch && atMinStep)): error 2.9e-3 at RelTol 1e-9, silent; live reports STIFF_SOLVER_STEP_TOO_SMALL and Simulink reports a min-step violation. Pinned in xbSolversB. Found by WP-12b.
findings.fix: WP-21 E13: batch ode23 / ode45 report STIFF_SOLVER_STEP_TOO_SMALL (error) when the tolerance is missed at minStep, as live does; a minStep step that straddles a zero crossing is located first.

findings.summary: Engine-level validation of maxStep / minStep is inconsistent: only batch ode23tb gives STIFF_SOLVER_INVALID_OPTION (and only for non-positive values); live maxStep <= 0 reports the misleading STIFF_SOLVER_STEP_TOO_SMALL; batch ode23 / ode45 clamp silently (maxStep 0 means ~1e6 steps); minStep > maxStep is silent. The canvas validates the same texts first, so only API and batch callers reach it. Pinned in xbSolversB. Found by WP-12b.
findings.fix: WP-21 E13: stepLimitProblem() gives STIFF_SOLVER_INVALID_OPTION for maxStep / minStep <= 0, non-finite, or minStep > maxStep in ode23 / ode45 / ode23tb, live and batch.

findings.summary: SolverOptions.stiffDetect and outputTimes (types.ts 118-119) are declared but read by no solver: remove them or implement them (as D3 removed ode113 / ode15s / ode23s). Neither Simulink nor MATLAB ode45 has a stiffness diagnostic. Pinned in xbSolversB. Found by WP-12b.
findings.fix: WP-21 E13: stiffDetect and outputTimes removed from SolverOptions (decision D19).

findings.summary: ode23tb batch with minStep = maxStep = 1e-3 (accepted by the canvas) on x' = -x stops with STIFF_SOLVER_STEP_TOO_SMALL at t = 0.498 / 0.998: rounding drift leaves a final step of remaining / 2, below minStep. The last step before an output or stop time must be allowed to be shorter than minStep (or merged with the previous one). Same before and after E13. Found by the E13 verifier.
findings.fix: WP-21 E14: ode23tb batch merges a remainder below minStep into the step when it fits within maxStep (1 + 1e-9), else halves only if the half stays >= minStep, else lets the last step before the target be the short one; minStep = maxStep = 1e-3 runs to stops 0.3337 / 1.0003 / 1 / 2.71828 with error <= 1.5e-8; genuine minStep violations (XBV-425, 2 MHz PWM, Saturation) still reported.

findings.summary: The E13 initial-step heuristic is not used in batch runs (Solvers.runFixedStep always fills fixedStep = span / 50, so the first step is span / 50 capped by maxStep; the error control then rejects it if too large) and is not recomputed after an event or reset, though the comment says so. Behaviour is correct but inefficient and the comment is wrong. Found by the E13 verifier.
findings.fix: WP-21 E14: Solvers.runFixedStep passes no fixedStep to ode23 / ode45 unless the user gave one, so the MATLAB initial step decides the first batch step (RelTol 1e-9: ode45 0.0126791, ode23 0.0008); ode23 exponent exactly -1/3; the comment no longer claims a recompute after events.

notes_for_later_wps.note: From the WP-04 verifier: integer overflow per data type, Gain matrix mode (K*u; ADIA only has element-wise, which is the Simulink default), exact degree values (sind(180) = 1.2e-16, tand(90) finite), Inf in Sum, PRODUCT with a single vector input (NaN, part of XBV-042).

From the WP-05 verifier, not yet pinned: Switch scalar expansion and vector ctrl; IF_ELSE with NaN (false) and [0] (true); MatrixConcat with unequal widths returns a ragged matrix; SubMatrix clamps out-of-range ends; MatrixSolve on a rank-deficient consistent system returns one solution silently; Inverse/Determinant of a non-square matrix throw (XBV-055 family); MatrixDiag ignores diagMode (auto-detects by shape); cond 1e12/1e16; single-input XOR; clock high at step 0 counted as an edge.

From WP-06: DERIVATIVE tau 0 or negative is replaced by 0.01 (instance of XBV-019); derivative of a Step under rk4 spikes at 83.3 (step seen at the mid stage of the previous step) - compare with Simulink Derivative in WP-15; INTERP_PRELOOKUP default table differs from LOOKUP_ND default; Flat/Nearest lookup require ExtrapMethod 'Clip' (linear extrapolation rejected) - check against Simulink.

From WP-08: IM_SCALAR_CONTROL ignores rated_f (no constant-voltage region above rated frequency) and uses |w_ref| (a negative command does not reverse the phase sequence); at w_ref = 0 it outputs a DC set of amplitude 10; THREE_PHASE_INVERTER ignores its Ron and Vf parameters; SVPWM 'Holtz 1992' over-modulation rule from the executor's memory - confirm in WP-15; factory `||` fallbacks such as Ts || 1e-4 not probed (XBV-019 covers them).

BAND_LIMITED_NOISE untested (Simulink: output variance = PSD / Ts); the 'trapezoidal' PID method is named 'tustin' in ADIA (trapezoidal rejected with PARAMETER_OPTION_INVALID) - naming check against Simulink; KF covariance read from nextState (P not an output).

From the WP-08 Opus verifier: six-step test cannot detect reversed torque or a 60-degree Hall advance (no Hall alignment oracle); AC motor ia+ib+ic = 0 is structural (ic = -ia - ib), so it is not evidence; field-weakening exact law needs a Simulink/MCB reference (WP-15).
CURRENT_CONTROLLER_DQ iMax scaling rule is taken from a factory comment, not an oracle - confirm against MCB in WP-15.
